Sterling.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the said Duty be, for every Piece of Vellum* Parchment, or Paper, upon which any common Bail or Appearance to be filed, entered, or registered, in any Court whatsoever, shall be ingrossed, written, or registered, the Sum of 6d. Sterling.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the said Duty be, for every Piece of Vellum, Parchment, or Paper, upon which shall be ingrossed or written any Rule or Order made or given in any the Courts at Westminster, either Courts of Law or Equity, or upon which shall be ingrossed, written, or registrat, any Interlocutory Rule, Order, or Act, of Court, made or given in the Courts of Session or Justiciary, Court of Exchequer, or any other of her Majesty’s Superior Courts in Scotland, the Smn of 6cL Sterling.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the said Duty be, for every Piece of Vellum, Parchment, or Paper, upon which any Copy of such Rule, Order, or Act of Court, shall be entered or registered, or the Copies of any oilier Records, Acts, Proceedings, or judicial Writs, or Writs belonging to the Execution of Sentences, in any of the said Courts, not otherwise charged, the Sum of 6d. Sterling. 1

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the said Duty be, for every Skin or Piece of Vellum, Parchment, or Paper, upon which shall be ingrossed or written any Citation or Monition made in, or Summons or other Mandate from, any Ecclesiastical Court, or Presbytery, or any Libel, or Allegation, Deposition, Answer, Sentence, or final Decree, or Inventory, exceeding ,£. 100. made, given, or exhibited, to or in any such Ecclesiastical Court, or Presbytery, or in any Court of Admiralty, or Cinque Ports, or any Court or Assembly exercising Spiritual or Admiralty Power or Jurisdiction, or whereupon any Copies of them respectively shall be ingrossed or written, the Sum of 6d. Sterling.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the said Duty be, for every Skin or Piece of Vellum or Parchment, or Sheet or Piece of Paper, upon Which shall be ingrossed or written any Charter-party, Policy of Insurance, Passport, Bond, Release, Contract, or other obligatory Instrument, or any Protest, Procuration, Letter of Attorney, or any other notarial Act whatsoever, in Great Britain, not otherwise charged, the Sum of 6d. Sterling.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That The said Duty be, for every Skin or Piece.of Vellum or Parchment, or Sheet or Piece of Paper, upon which shall be ingrossed or written any Declaration, Plea, Replication, Rejoinder, Demurrer, or other Pleading whatsoever, in any Court of Law in England, Wales, or Beneick upon Ticeed; or upon which shall be im grossed, written, or registrat, any Libel, Allegation, Plea, Reply, Duply, Interrogatory, Deposition, or other Pleading, or Writ, either by way of Allegation or Proof, on behalf of any Party litigant, in any Court or Session in Scotland, not otherwise charged; the Sum of id. Sterling.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the said Duty be, for every Skin or Piece of Vellum, Parchment, or Paper, upon which any Copy of any of them shall be ingrossed or written, the Sum of 1 d> Sterling.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the said Duty be, for every Skin or Piece of Velr lum> or Parchment, or Sheet or Piece of Paper, upon which any Depositions taken in the Court of Chancery, or other Court ,of Equity; except the Paper Draughts of Depositions, taken by virtue of any Commission, before they are ingrossed; or upon which any Copy of any Bill, Answer, Plea, Demurrer, Replication, Rejoinder, Interrogatories, Depositions, or other Proceedings whatsoever, in any Court of Equity, shall be ingrossed or written; the Sum of One Peny Sterling.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That where more than One of any the Matters or Things aforesaid shall be ingrossed, written, entered, or registered, upon One Piece of Vellum, Parchment, or Paper, the said respective Duties be charged upon every One of such Matters and Things respectively.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That all Vellum, Parchment, and Paper, to be charged as aforesaid, and which hath been already stamped, in pursuance of the former Acts of Parliament relating to her Majesty’s Stamp-duties, shall, before any the said Matters or Things be written or ingrossed thereupon, such Writing or Ingrossing being after the First Day of August 1714, be brought to be stamped with a Third Mark or Impression; and that all such Vellum, Parchment, and Paper, which shall, after that Day, not have been stamped, pursuant to the said former Acts, shall, before the said Matters or Things be written or im-grossed thereupon, such Writing or-Ingrossing being after the said First Day of August 1714, be brought to be stamped with such Marks or Impressions, as may properly denote the Duties charged thereupon.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the additional Duties upon Soap and Paper, and upon certain Linens, Silks, Callicoes, and Stuffs, and upon Transfers of Stocks, and upon Starch, and upon stampt Vellum, Parchment, and Paper, be granted to her Majesty lor the Term of 32 Years.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion, of this Committee, That a Fund of JO. 112,500. per Annum, for 32 Years, be settled and established, and charged: upon, and made payable out of, all the said additional Duties, for raising the Sum of £. 1,500,000. by way of a Lottery.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, towards the Supply granted to her Majesty, the Money which is unappropriated, or that shall arise out of the Surplusages, on Accounts paid into the Exciter quer, be applied to the current Service of this Year.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, for the further Encouragement of the LeatherMa-inifacture in this Kingdom,a Drawback of the whole Duty of One Peny Halfpeny per Pound Weight be allowed on all tanned Leather, which slpdl be manufactured and actually made into Goods or Wares, and exported out of Great Britain, to be ascertained, according to the Weight of such Wares or Goods respectively.

3d, Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, towards railing the Supply granted to her Majesty, a further Duty be laid upon such Vellum, Parchment, and Paper, whereupon certain Matters or Things shall be ingrossed or written; over and above all Duties already chargeable on them, or any of tlrem.

4th, Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the said Duty be, for every Skin or Piece of Vellum or Parchment, on which any Grants, or Letters Patents, under the Great Seal of Great Britain, or the Seal of the Duchy or County Palatine of Lancajer, of any Honour, Dignity, Promotion, Franchise, Liberty, or Privilege, to any Person or Persons, Bodies Politick or Corporate, or Exemplifications of the fame, shall be ingrossed or written, Commissions of Rebellion in Process always excepted, the Sum of 40 s.

5th, Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the said Duty be, for every Skin or Piece of Vellum or Parchment, or Sheet or Piece of Paper, on which any Pardon, except the general Circuits, and Newgate Pardons, of or for any Crime or Offence, or of any Sum of Money, or Forfeiture, whatsoever, or on which any Warrant of Reprieve, or Relaxation from any Pecuniary Fine, or Forfeiture, exceeding £. 100, or from any corporal Punishment, shall be ingrossed or written, the Sum of 40 s.Sterling.

6th, Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the said Duty be, for every Skin or Piece of Vellum or Parchment, or Sheet or Piece of Paper, upon which any Grant from her Majesty, her Heirs or Successors, of any Sum of Money exceeding f. 100 Sterling, which shall pass the Great Seal of Great Britain, the Great Seal of Scotland, or the Privy Seal, not directed to the Great Seal, shall be ingrossed or written, the Sum of 40 s. Sterling.

7th, Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the said Duty be, for every Skin or Piece of Vellum or Parchment, or Sheet or Piece of Paper, upon which any Grant of any Office or Employment in Great Britain, which shall be above the Value of 50 Sterling per Annum, shall be ingrossed or written, the Sum of 40 s. Sterling.

8th, Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the said Duty be, for every Skin or Piece of Vellum or Parchment, or Sheet or Piece of Paper, upon which any Difpeufation to hold two Ecclesiastical Dignities or Benefices, or both a Dignity and a Benefice, or any other Dispensation, or Faculty, from the Lord Archbishop of Canterbury, or the Mailer of the Faculties, for the Time being, shall be ingrossed or written, the Sum of Forty Shillings Sterling.

9th, Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the said Duty be, for every Skin or Piece of Vellum or Parchment, or Sheet or Piece of Paper, upon which shall be ingrossed or written any Admittance, or Instrument for admitting, of any Fellow of the College of Physicians, or of any Attorney, Clerk, Advocate, Proctor, Notary, or other Officer or Officers, in any Court - whatsoever, in Great Britain, not being an annual Officer in any Corporation, or inferior Court, whose Office is under the Value of £. 10 Sterling per Annum in Salary, Fees, or other Perquisites, the Sum of 40 s. Sterling.

10th, Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the said Duty be, for every Skin or Piece of Vellum or Parchment, or Sheet or Piece of Paper, upon Which any Appeal from the High Courts of Admiralty, either in England or Scotland, Court of Arches, or the Vpi. 17.

The House, according to Order, resumed the adjourn-" ed Confederation of the Report of the Bill for the more effectual Punishment of Vagrants, and fending them whither they ought to he sent.

And Clause B, upon which the further Consideration of the Report was adjourned, was amended; and, upon the Question put thereupon, agreed unto by the House.

A Clause was offered, to be added to the Bill, That the Charge of conveying such Persons as are found, upon a general privy Search, to have committed such Acts of Vagrancy, and to have no fixed Abode, or Employment, shall be defrayed in the same manner as the Charge of conveying other Rogues and Vagabonds sent to the Place of their Birth is to be defrayed:

And the same was twice read; and, upon the Question put thereupon, agreed unto by the House to be made Part of the Bill.

Another Clause was offered, to be added to the Bill,

That or more Justices of Peace may, by Warrant under directed to the Constables, Church-

wardens, and Overseers of the Poor, of any Parish or Place, cause any Persons, of little or no Estates, who, by Lunacy or otherwise, are furiously mad, and dangerous to be permitted to go abroad, to be apprehended, and kept safely locked up, where such Justices shall appoint; but the Ad shall... abridge the Prerogative of the Queen, or Power of the Lord Chancellor:

And the same was twice read, with Blanks; which were filled up:

And then the Clause was, upon the Question put thereupon, agreed unto by the House to be made Part of the Bill.

Another Clause was offered, to be added to the Bill, That if Persons shall be found by Confection, or by Oath, Witnesses, to have obtained no legal Settlement fmee their Birth, the Justice, instead ofpunishing them, shall commit them to the Custody of any other Person willing to receive them, as Apprentices or Servants, for Years; who may set them to work in Great Britain, or in any her Majesty's Plantations; but none shall be transported till Security shall be given of such their Transportation:

And the same was twice read, with Blanks; which were filled up:

And then the Clause was, upon the Question put thereupon, agreed unto by the House to be made Part of the Bill.

Another Clause was offered, to be added to the Bill, relating to the Conveyance of Soldiers from Sea-ports: And the Question being put, That the Clause be brought up to the Table;

It passed in the Negative.

And other Amendments were made by the House to the Bill.

Ordered, That the Bill, with the Amendments, be ingrossed.

Mr. Medlycot reported, according to Order, from the Harwich Committee of Privileges and Elections, the Matter, as E1*&ot it appeared to them, touching the Election for the Borough of Hanoich, in the County of Essex, and the Resolutions of the Committee thereupon} which they had directed him to report to the House; and be read the Report in his Plaec; and afterwards delivered the same in at the Clerk’s Table: Where the same was read: And the Report, and Resolutions, are as follow; viz.

Upon the Petition of BenediS Leonard Calvert Esquire, complaining of an undue Election and Return of Thomas Heath Esquire, to serve for the Borough of Harwich, in the County of Essex:

That the Right of Election was agreed to be in the Mayor, Aldermen, and Capital Burgesses, or Head-boroughs, residing within the Borough:

That the Poll was,

19 for Mr. Heath:

12 for Mr. Calvert.

That the Petitioner’s Counsel alleged, They should add Charles Smith to their Poll; and take off 13 from the Sitting Member’s Poll; viz. John Phillips and Win. Jeffery, for not being duly elected; the said Phillips, and Six others, for not being qualified according to the Corporation Act; and Two of those Six, and Five others, for Bribery.

It appeared by the Town-book, That Charles Smith was elected and sworn a Capital Burgess upon the l6tfi of October 1712: And,

Daniel Smyth junior said, That, Two Years ago,

Charles Smyth was Storekeeper at; and, at the

time of this Election, had Lodgings, and Clothes, and Books, and a Chest, there} though, at the same time, he

That it appeared, by Two Instruments, signed by the Capital Burgesses, That, at a great Court, held the 15th of February last, Mr. John Philips and Mr. Wm. jef-J'eiyes were putin Nomination, and Election of a Capital Burgess, in the room and place of Mr. Charles Smyth, who is amoved: That Two voted for Philips, and Three for Jefferyes; and that Ten others of the Aldermen and

Capital Burgesses protested against the Amoval of Smyth, as being without sufficient Reason; and the Court illegal, and contrary to the Charter and Constitutions of the Borough; by which the Mayor cannot keep a Court without the Recorder, or Steward, or sworn Deputy, or One of them. And

Daniel Smyth junior said, That neither the Reoorder, nor Steward, nor Deputy Steward, were present ^t this Court; and that he never knew a Court held without One of those Officers present.

That the Petitioner's Counsel objected against the said John Philips and Six others of the Sitting Member’s Voters, as disqualified by the Corporation Act; viz. Henty Luff kin, elected the 10th, and sworn the 15th of December 1713:.

Mr. Wm. Curteis said, He was instituted Vicar of Harwich in October 1706; and, ever ft nee that time, has himself administered all the Sacraments which have been received there; and usually took Memorandums of the Persons receiving, that he might certify tlieiji to the Quarter Sessions, if they desired it:

That the Seven Persons before-named did receive the Sacrament from him within Three Months after their Election into Office; but none of them within the Year before such Election:

Being cross-examined, he said, He had a Curate at Dover Court, >vho officiated there for, him a Year and a Quarter; and what Persons received the Sacrament there in that time, or whether any of these might not receive it elsewhere, he could not tell; but said, They are all constant Churchmen; and that he never knew any of them to go to a Dissenting Meeting.

To take off Two of the aforesaid Voters; viz. John Fennings, and Giles Baker, and Five others, for Bribery; the Petitioner’s Counsel called,

Philip Trahern: Who said. That, upon the 12th of May last, being the Wednesday before the Election, which was upon the 17th of May, he went to Harwich to serve Process of the Sheriff of Essex upon one Mr. Ewer, who was going to Holland; on which Occasion, he went to fee his old Acquaintance Robert Kebell; and inquired out several of the Sitting Member’s Voters, who confessed to him the following Bribes; viz.

Robert Kebell said, The Sitting Member had promised him a considerable Sum; and that he had already received £.20 of him for his Vote:

John Dean said, The Sitting Member had promised to provide for his Son-in-law; and that he had received Ten Guineas for, his Vote already; and expected Ten more, when the Election was over:

Joseph Mum said. The Sitting Member was the bell

Vol. 17.

Friend he had in the World; that he had of him, upon the last Election, One hundred and odd Pounds to pay offa Bond to Sir Thomas Davall; but now he had only Ten Guineas; and that Mr. Heath should have his Vote as long as he stood:

Richard Carrington told him,. That, upon the last Election, he had £.20, and was promised £.10 for his Vote now; and could have an old Coach-horse of the Sitting Member at any time;

John Fennings, whose Business is to look for loft An* chore, said, He was promised to be helped to a Merchant, who would bby all his Anchors; and that he had a Present of Five Guineas for his Vote in this Election, which came from the Sitting Member, or his Lady; but he could not tell from which:

Robert Stephens said, He always used to vote for the other Side; that he had made as much of his Vote as he copld, and did not care which Side carried it; and that he had received 20 Guineas of the Sitting Member for his Vote in this Election:

Giles Baker said, The Sitting Member had been his Friend; and had gone £.50 Part of his Vessel; but they could make nothing of that; for it was no Bribery, he was sure.

By the Report of the last controverted Election, produced by the Sitting Member’s Counsel; it apj peared. That

Mr. Daniel Smyth senior, being then examined as a Witness, said, " He had been Steward of the Borough " above 40 Years: That the Right of Election is in the " Mayor, Aldermen, and Capital Burgesses, or Headboroughs, refidingwithin the Borough, sand no others:'

" It had been always practised, that, when a Capital’ " Burgess totally leaves the Town, and has no Family " or Relideuce there, beceafes to be a Capital Burgess: ' " They make no Order for disfranchising him; but his' " Place is, ipso facto,\oid; and he mentioned the several " Instances of this Practice above 20 Years ago, in the " Cafes of Sir Anthony Dean, Robert Fox, Isaac Betts,

" Stephen Morrife, Captain Radburn, and Edmund " Reynolds-, on whose Removal others were chosen in " their Places:" And,

Being cross-examined; he said, Captain Burleigh,

" after he removed out of Town, acted as a Capital *s Burgess; but then the Non-residents were not disputed; and that Charles Smyth his Nephew, and " Daniel Smyth his Son, acted as Capital Burgesses,' " although they resided as Lodgers in the Town."’

And the Committee then came to a Resolution, to which the House afterwards agreed, " That the Right of " Election of Burgesses to serve in Parliament for this " Borough, is in the Mayor, Aldermen, and Capital " Burgesses, or Headboroughs, of the Borough, residing within the Borough."

Charles Smyth was also objected against; for that the Oath of Office was not administered to him at the great Court, which the Charter requires.

That the Petitioner’s Counsel admitted the Charter directs the Burgesses to be sworn at the great Court; but infilled, That Charles Smyth was well sworn, though at his Lodgings; the Oath being the re administered to him by virtue of an Order of the great Court for that Purpose, upon the Accident of breaking his Leg.

The Committee came to the following Resolutions; via.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That Mr. John Ord, having, by Robert Burrell his Clerk, upon the 24th Day of May lall, delivered a Declaration in Ejectment, in the Court of Pleas at Durham, for a Wharf and Appurtenances, in the Parish of Wickham, in the County of Durham, in the Possession of George Pitt Esquire, a Member of this House, is guilty of a Breach of the Privilege of this House.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee That the said Robert Burrell, having delivered the said Declaration in lyeftment, is guilty of a Breach of the Privilege of this House.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That Wm.Ramsay Esquire, the Lessor of the Plaintiff in

the said Ejectment, is guilty of a Breach of the Privilege of this House.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That Mr. John Mowbray, the Attorney upon Record in the said iyeftment, is guilty of a Breach of the Privilege of this House.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That Philip Hazard, Nicholas Spark, and Henry Taylor, having, upon the 29th Day of June last, arrested several of the said Mr. Pitt's Servants and Workmen, in divers

Actions brought, touching the said Wharf and Appurtenances in the said Mr. Pitt's Possession, are guilty of a Breach of the Privilege of this House.

The said Resolutions, being severally read a Second time, were, upon the Question severally put thereupon, agreed unto by the House.

Ordered, That the said Mr. John Ord, Robert Burrell, William Ramsay Esquire, Mr. John Mowbray, Philip Hazard, Nicholas Spark, and Henry Taylor, be, for their said several Offences, taken into the Custody of the Serjeant at Arms attending this House.

A. 1714.

A Message from her Majesty, by Sir William Oldes, Gentleman Usher of the Black nod:

Mr. Speaker,

The. Queen commands this honourable House to attend her Majesty, in the House of Peers, immediately.

Accordingly, Mr. Speaker, with the House, went up to attend her Majesty, in the House of Peers: Where her Majesty was pleased to give the Royal Assent to several publick and private Bills:

After which her Majesty was pleased to make a most gracious Speech to both Houses of Parliament:

And afterwards the Lord High Chancellor of Great Britain, by her Majesty’s Command, said

My Lords, and Gentlemen,

It is her Majesty’s Royal Will and Pleasure, That this Parliament be prorogued to Tuesday the Tenth Day of August next: And this Parliament is accordingly prorogued to Tuesday the Tenth Day of August next.

90 Julii.
